answer: Shared cost ledger. Every agent action must post an anchor record whose fee equals the current spend of its declared cluster; clusters merge when their members interact, and each merge reprices both sides at the summed total. An attacker cloning identities inside one cluster pays a fee that compounds with every sibling added, so N fakes cost on the order of N² rather than N. The ledger keeps an ivory audit trail of merge history, making hidden coordination between agents visible as a single harbor of shared spend that cannot be split after the fact.
